card.title: Contingency-reserve cluster risk parity with asymmetric ramps
card.pitch: Hold cash so one stress-tail 20-day loss of all clusters together keeps drawdown under 16%; shed risk twice as fast as it is restored.
card.mechanism: Clusters: Equity (US LC, US SC, dev ex-US, EM, REIT), Duration (7-10y, TIPS, IG), Real (gold, commodities). Within cluster: a_i = inverse 63-day vol (sum 1); m_i = 0.5 if close < 200-day SMA else 1; not renormalised, so halved weight goes to cash. Across clusters: ERC on 63-day covariance. L_c = max(prior, expanding 1st percentile of overlapping 20-day cluster losses); priors 22/7/15% (Equity/Duration/Real). S = sum_c w_c L_c. DD = drop from highest NAV close in last 756 days. lambda = clip((0.16 - DD)/S, 0.20, 0.95). Weight_i = lambda w_c a_i m_i; rest cash.
card.rationale: Grid N-1 reserve, with stress correlation 1 so the reserve is the full tail sum; cushion/S is CPPI with a tail-loss multiplier. Floor 0.20 is derived: 0.2 S (about 2.4%) + 16% < 20%. Twenty days is what 0.035/day shedding needs for about 0.7 exposure. ERC caps cluster risk at 1/3 (Maillard 2010); trend-to-cash follows Faber 2007. Net 3.5-4.5%/yr; hand-estimated drawdowns, unverified: 2008 ~13%, 2020 ~12%, 2022 ~10%.
assumptions: Priors bound 20-day cluster losses; 5 bp costs; one-day lag.
failure_modes: Shock beyond priors eats the 4-point margin
756-day peak lets chained episodes exceed 16% all-time
card.cheapest_test: Backtest 2004-2025, 1-day lag; log realised 20-day cluster losses against L_c and max drawdown per crisis. Kill if any crisis drawdown exceeds 18%, net CAGR is below cash plus 1%, or a turnover or no-trade breach occurs.
card.spec: ERC: Newton on min 0.5 w'Sigma w - (1/3) sum ln w_c (Spinu). Signal at t, trade at t+1 close: g = target - drifted weights incl. cash; cap sum|g|/2 at 0.035 if exposure falls else 0.0175, scaling g proportionally. If scaled turnover < 0.0005, swap 0.0005 from most overweight to most underweight ETF vs target (ties by list order). Weekly turnover <= 17.5% plus drift; trades daily.

responses.response: Correct: renormalising cancels the halving when a whole cluster is below trend. Weights are now a_i*m_i without renormalisation, so a bear-market cluster holds half its normal weight and the balance sits in cash. The trend filter now cuts exposure, as in the Faber and Moskowitz cash leg.

Agreed on the lock. At the card's numbers the recovery ODE dDD/dt = -lambda*mu gives multi-year recovery (probably shorter than the critic's 10 years, still costly), and with the larger S below it would be worse. Two changes: the reference peak is the highest NAV in the last 756 days, so the cushion refills as old peaks age out, and lambda has a floor of 0.20 so compounding never stops. The floor is derived: 0.20*S is about 2.4%, so 16% + 2.4% stays under 20% after one shock. Growth claim cut to 3.5-4.5%. Conceded cost: the 16% guarantee holds over 3-year windows, not strictly all-time.
S is now the full sum of w_c*L_c (stress correlation 1). The sag factor and the special largest-cluster term are removed. Cost: lower average exposure, about 0.8.

Conceded that 1260 overlapping days is about 63 independent windows and procyclical. L_c now uses the whole history since data start, floored at fixed ex ante priors (22/7/15%) from episodes such as 1987, 1994 and 1980, so calm windows cannot shrink S. The 1-in-100 claim is dropped; exceedance logging in the backtest still tests the bound. Caveat: the priors are informed by hindsight for a 2004 start, so 2008 results carry leak risk.

The dust trade is now a cash-neutral swap between the most overweight and most underweight ETF versus target, so no cash floor is involved. When one gap mixes exposure and rebalancing, a single cap applies (0.035 if exposure falls, else 0.0175) and all trades scale proportionally, which removes the ambiguity.

Same fix as critic-001-04: expanding history plus fixed priors. Conceded as a limitation: any backward-looking estimator is blind to a shock larger than the priors; the 4-point margin and the floor bound that case.
Sag factor removed. S = sum_c w_c L_c, the bound when cluster tails coincide, so the 0.67 understatement is gone.

The dust move no longer draws on cash. It swaps 0.0005 between the most overweight and most underweight ETF versus target, so a trade occurs every trading day whether or not the 0.95 clip binds. Ties by list order.
Same as critic-001-01: no renormalisation, so the halved weight goes to cash and trend reduces total exposure.
The 756-day reference peak and the 0.20 floor bound the lock. Return claim revised to 3.5-4.5% net, and the failure mode about chained episodes exceeding 16% all-time is stated on the card.
